channel.title: Ajna Consulting Services — Insights
channel.description: Enterprise architecture, cloud, AI and MLOps writing from Ajna Consulting Services.

item.title: Platform Observability: Building the Visibility Layer Every Application Team Gets Automatically
item.description: How platform teams build and operate the metrics, logging, and tracing infrastructure that application teams consume without configuring — and what good platform observability coverage actually looks like.

item.title: Neural Networks Explained: What They Are, How They Learn, and Why They Work
item.description: Neurons, layers, weights, activation functions, backpropagation, and gradient descent — the actual mechanics of how a neural network learns from data, explained without the mathematics becoming the obstacle.

item.title: RAG, Prompting, and Building Applications on LLMs: The Practitioner's Guide
item.description: Retrieval-augmented generation, system prompts, few-shot examples, chain-of-thought, structured output, and the engineering patterns that make LLM applications reliable in production.

item.title: Putting AI in Production: What Enterprise AI Deployment Actually Requires
item.description: Model serving, latency, cost, monitoring, governance, and the operational discipline that separates a proof of concept from an AI system that runs reliably at enterprise scale.

item.title: What Containers Actually Are — Not the Marketing Version
item.description: Containers are not lightweight VMs. They are processes with resource constraints and namespace isolation. Understanding the actual mechanism makes you a better user of Docker, Kubernetes, and every container runtime.

item.title: Measuring Platform Engineering Success: The Metrics That Actually Matter
item.description: DORA metrics, developer experience scores, cognitive load measures, and the platform health indicators that tell you whether your internal platform is creating value or creating another bottleneck.

item.title: Cloud Cost Anomaly Detection: Catching Runaway Spend Before It Becomes a Bill
item.description: Cloud cost overruns that show up in the monthly invoice are already weeks old. Here's how to set up anomaly detection that catches cost spikes in hours, with enough context to diagnose the cause quickly.

item.title: Writing Production-Grade Dockerfiles: The Decisions That Actually Matter
item.description: Multi-stage builds, minimal base images, layer caching, non-root users, build arguments, and the specific Dockerfile patterns that separate a working image from a secure, efficient, maintainable one.

item.title: Cloud Tagging Policy Template: The Foundation FinOps Actually Requires
item.description: A tagging policy that nobody enforces is worse than no tagging policy. Here's how to design a tagging taxonomy that survives contact with real engineering teams — with enforcement mechanisms, exceptions handling, and the tags that actually drive cost allocation decisions.

item.title: Linux Namespaces and cgroups: The Foundation of Containers
item.description: How Linux namespaces isolate processes, filesystems, networks, and users — and how cgroups enforce resource limits. The primitives that Docker, Kubernetes, and every container runtime are built on.

item.title: Designing an Internal Developer Platform: Abstraction Layers, Golden Paths, and the Governance Balance
item.description: How to design the abstraction layer between your platform and your application teams — what to hide, what to expose, and how to build the golden paths that make good practices the easy practices.

item.title: Self-Service Infrastructure: How to Build It Without Losing Operational Control
item.description: Scaffolding tools, infrastructure templates, self-service portals, and the approval workflows that give developers autonomy without turning the platform into a liability.

item.title: Container Networking: How Containers Talk to Each Other and to the Outside World
item.description: Bridge networks, overlay networks, DNS-based service discovery, port publishing, and the iptables rules that make container networking work — and fail.

item.title: Kubernetes Security Hardening: The Controls That Actually Reduce Attack Surface
item.description: Default Kubernetes configurations are not production-secure. Here are the specific hardening controls — RBAC, Pod Security Standards, network policies, image policies, secrets management — that reduce attack surface and what each actually protects against.

item.title: Back-of-Envelope Engineering: The Estimation Skill That Filters Bad Architectures in Minutes
item.description: Before the design review argues about frameworks, arithmetic should have eliminated half the options. The latency numbers worth memorizing, the estimation moves — traffic, storage, bandwidth, cost — and worked habits that turn guesses into engineering.

item.title: Deployment Strategies Compared: Rolling, Blue-Green, Canary, and When Each Actually Fits
item.description: Rolling updates, blue-green switches, canary releases, and shadow traffic — what each strategy really costs, what each protects against, and the database problem that constrains all of them.

item.title: Modernizing Legacy Java: A Roadmap from Java 8 to 21+ Without Stopping the Business
item.description: Most enterprise Java still runs on versions the ecosystem has left behind. A staged roadmap for moving Java 8 estates to 21+ — what breaks, what to automate, how to sequence framework upgrades, and how to sell the work to the business.

item.title: Virtual Threads in the Enterprise: What Changes, What Doesn't, and What Breaks
item.description: Java 21's virtual threads promise massive concurrency without reactive complexity. Here's what actually changes in enterprise services — thread pool math, pinning pitfalls, connection pools as the new bottleneck, and when reactive still wins.

item.title: Multi-Region Architecture Patterns: What You're Actually Buying at Each Tier
item.description: Active-passive, pilot light, active-active, and the data problem underneath them all. A tiered framework for multi-region design that matches architecture to actual availability requirements — and prices the tiers honestly.

item.title: Queueing Theory for Engineers: Why Everything Melts at 80% Utilization
item.description: Little's Law, the utilization-latency curve, and variability's tax — the three results that explain most capacity mysteries, from connection pools to on-call load. No calculus required, just the intuitions that make systems behavior predictable.

item.title: The Strangler Fig in Practice: Incremental Legacy Replacement That Actually Finishes
item.description: Everyone cites the strangler pattern; few finish a strangulation. The facade and routing mechanics, the data-migration sequencing that makes or breaks it, the organizational funding model, and the anti-patterns that leave estates half-strangled forever.

item.title: Designing for Failure: Resilience Patterns That Actually Hold in Production
item.description: Circuit breakers, bulkheads, retry logic, chaos engineering — the resilience patterns that genuinely reduce MTTR and the ones that look good on architecture diagrams but fail when things get real.

item.title: PostgreSQL Performance Tuning: The Settings and Patterns That Actually Matter
item.description: PostgreSQL's default configuration is conservative, designed for small deployments. For production workloads, the settings that control memory, parallelism, WAL behavior, and connection handling need explicit tuning. Here's where to start.

item.title: AI Cost Management in Production: Controlling Token Spend Without Degrading Quality
item.description: LLM API costs scale with usage in ways that surprise teams used to fixed infrastructure pricing. Here's how to build cost visibility, set sensible ceilings, and optimize prompt design without breaking the features that depend on it.

item.title: Kubernetes Fundamentals: What It Is, What It Does, and When You Actually Need It
item.description: Pods, Deployments, Services, ConfigMaps, and the control loop that keeps your containers running. The honest introduction to Kubernetes for engineers who want to understand it, not just use it.

item.title: Reserved Instance Rationalisation: How to Commit to the Right Resources
item.description: Committed use discounts (Reserved Instances, Savings Plans, CUDs) are one of the highest-return FinOps actions — but committing to the wrong shape or term locks in waste. Here's the analysis process for getting it right.

item.title: GCP Cost Management: Committed Use Discounts, Recommenders, and What Cloud Billing Doesn't Show You
item.description: Google Cloud's cost optimization tools are extensive but spread across multiple products. Here's how Committed Use Discounts, the Recommender API, and billing export to BigQuery work together for a complete FinOps practice.

item.title: Software Supply Chain Security: SBOM, Dependency Auditing, and What Actually Reduces Risk
item.description: The software supply chain attack surface is large and growing. SBOMs, dependency scanning, and provenance verification are the practical measures that reduce real risk — here's what each covers and where the gaps are.

item.title: Cloud Unit Economics: The Metric That Makes Cloud Spend Conversations Productive
item.description: Talking about cloud spend in absolute dollars rarely leads anywhere useful. Unit economics — cost per transaction, cost per user, cost per GB processed — creates the context that turns 'we spend too much on cloud' into an actionable conversation.

item.title: Structured Logging That Pays for Itself: Schema, Context, and Cost Discipline
item.description: Logs are the most expensive telemetry most organizations run and the least designed. Event schemas, correlation context, level discipline, sampling, and the cost engineering that keeps the logging bill from becoming the observability program's obituary.

item.title: Trace Sampling: Keeping the Traces That Matter When You Can't Keep Them All
item.description: Distributed tracing at production volume is a sampling problem wearing an instrumentation costume — head vs tail sampling, the consistency rules that keep traces whole, error-and-latency-biased retention, and the cost architecture of an honest tracing pipeline.

item.title: WebLogic Domains, Clusters, and Managed Servers: The Architecture Explained
item.description: Admin servers, managed servers, clusters, machines, and Node Manager — the WebLogic domain model explained for people who have to run it, not just pass the exam. What each piece does, how they fit together, and where production deployments go wrong.

item.title: WebLogic JMS in Production: Servers, Stores, and the Configuration That Survives Failover
item.description: JMS servers, persistent stores, distributed destinations, and connection factories — how WebLogic messaging actually fits together, and the configuration decisions that determine whether your queues survive a server failure.

item.title: WebLogic Performance Tuning: Work Managers, Connection Pools, and the Knobs That Actually Matter
item.description: A field guide to tuning WebLogic Server in production — the self-tuning thread pool, work managers, JDBC connection pools, JVM settings, and the diagnostic tools that tell you which knob to turn.

item.title: Database Replication Patterns: Read Replicas, Multi-Primary, and When Each Applies
item.description: Database replication serves two distinct goals — high availability (survive a primary failure) and read scaling (distribute read traffic). The configuration that optimizes for one is often wrong for the other.

item.title: What Machine Learning Actually Is — Before the Hype and After the Buzzwords
item.description: A precise definition of machine learning, the difference between supervised, unsupervised, and reinforcement learning, and why understanding the category matters before choosing an approach.

item.title: Why Cloud Migrations Fail: The Pattern Behind the Common Failures
item.description: Cloud migrations that fail share recognisable patterns — lift-and-shift with no optimization, underestimated dependency complexity, inadequate cost modeling. Understanding these patterns before starting is preventable failure.

item.title: Database Migration Strategies: Moving Production Data Without Downtime
item.description: Zero-downtime database migrations are possible but require discipline — dual-write patterns, schema compatibility phases, and a rollback plan that you've actually tested. Here's what works at production scale.

item.title: The MTTR Reduction Playbook: Investments That Actually Move the Needle
item.description: Mean Time to Recover is a lagging indicator — improving it requires leading investments in observability, runbooks, team practice, and architecture. Here's how to structure those investments and measure whether they're working.

item.title: Running LLMs Locally: What Six Months of Daily Use Actually Taught Me
item.description: I started running local LLMs as a cost experiment. It became a privacy practice, a performance benchmark, and an education in what language models actually need to function well. Here's the honest version of what I found.
